senses.gloss: To cover a surface with a thin layer of ice, or to give glass a cloudy white finish.
examples: Overnight the cold *frosted* every windshield on the block.
Ice *frosts* the inside of that old freezer within a week.
The shower door is *frosted* so no one can see through it.

senses.gloss: To stop a plan or an effort from succeeding.
examples: High winds *frustrated* the rescue attempt.
The new rules are meant to *frustrate* money laundering.
Their plans have been *frustrated* by a lack of money.

senses.gloss: To ruin an electrical device by overheating it or running too much current through it (informal).
examples: A power surge *fried* the router.
Too much voltage will *fry* the chip.
He has *fried* two laptops this year.

senses.gloss: To make someone feel satisfied and complete.
examples: Teaching *fulfills* her in a way that office work never did.
He quit because the job no longer *fulfilled* him.
Raising her kids has been the most *fulfilling* work of her life.

senses.gloss: To drop the ball or fail to hold on to it, especially in football.
senses.ru: упускать мяч, потерять мяч (в американском футболе)
examples: The running back *fumbled* on the five-yard line.
If you *fumble* inside your own twenty, you lose the game.
A *fumbled* snap gave Dallas the ball back.

senses.gloss: To coat iron or steel with zinc so that it will not rust.
examples: The plant *galvanizes* sheet metal by dipping it in molten zinc.
They *galvanized* the frame before shipping it north.
Use *galvanized* nails outdoors or they will streak the wood.

senses.gloss: To take a risk in the hope that something will turn out well.
examples: The studio *gambled* on an unknown director and it paid off.
We're *gambling* that the weather holds through Saturday.
You *gamble* a lot when you buy a house sight unseen.

senses.gloss: To take money out of someone's pay or bank account by court order to settle a debt.
senses.ru: удерживать (часть зарплаты) в счёт долга, налагать арест (на счёт)
examples: The court *garnished* his wages for unpaid child support.
Creditors can *garnish* up to a quarter of a paycheck.
Her account had already been *garnished* twice.

senses.gloss: To understand or conclude something from what you have seen or heard.
examples: I *gather* you two have already met.
From her voice he *gathered* that the news was bad.
We had *gathered* as much from her email.

senses.gloss: To shine with a light so strong that it hurts the eyes.
examples: The afternoon sun *glared* off the hood of the car.
Headlights *glare* badly on wet pavement.
She squinted at the *glaring* white of the snow.

senses.gloss: To look warm and healthy, or to show happiness in your face.
examples: She *glowed* with pride when they called her name.
His cheeks *glow* after a run in cold weather.
The new parents were *glowing* all evening.

senses.gloss: To charge someone a grossly unfair price.
examples: Hotels *gouged* travelers the week after the storm.
State law bars stores from *gouging* customers during an emergency.
Shops near the pier *gouge* tourists all summer.

senses.gloss: To control or decide how something works, said of a rule, a law, or a force.
examples: Federal law *governs* how the grant money can be spent.
The terms *governing* the loan are in section four.
For years, habit *governed* everything he did.

senses.gloss: To get or take something quickly and without fuss (informal).
examples: Let's *grab* a coffee before the meeting.
We *grabbed* a quick lunch at the airport.
I'm *grabbing* a seat near the front.

senses.gloss: To catch and hold someone's interest.
examples: The first chapter really *grabs* you.
The movie never *grabbed* me.
Headlines are written to *grab* your attention.

senses.gloss: To sort products into levels of quality or size.
examples: Inspectors *grade* the beef before it leaves the plant.
The eggs are *graded* by size and then packed.
They *graded* the lumber into three classes.

senses.gloss: To move skin, bone, or other living tissue from one part of the body to another in surgery.
examples: Surgeons *grafted* skin from his thigh onto the burn.
Doctors can *graft* bone taken from the hip.
The new tissue was *grafted* in place last week.

senses.gloss: To admit that something is true, even when it does not change your opinion.
examples: I'll *grant* you that the price is high.
She *granted* the point and moved on.
*Granted*, the weather could have been better.

senses.gloss: To rub against something with a harsh scraping sound, or to be irritating to hear.
examples: The heavy door *grated* as it swung open.
His laugh *grates* after about an hour.
Metal *grating* against metal woke the whole street.

senses.gloss: To react to news or to someone's work in a particular way.
examples: The announcement was *greeted* with boos.
Fans *greeted* the trade with relief.
Voters *greet* every tax hike with anger.

senses.gloss: To question someone long and hard.
examples: Reporters *grilled* the mayor for an hour.
Senators are *grilling* the nominee today.
My parents *grill* me about my grades every Sunday.

senses.gloss: To hold someone's attention or feelings completely.
examples: The story *grips* you from the first page.
The trial *gripped* the whole country for a month.
It's a *gripping* documentary about the 1980s.

senses.gloss: To train and prepare someone for an important job or role.
examples: The party *grooms* candidates years in advance.
They *groomed* her for a seat on the board.
He is being *groomed* as the next CEO.

senses.gloss: To connect electrical equipment to the earth so that it is safe to use.
examples: Always *ground* the equipment before you test it.
The old outlet was never *grounded*.
A copper rod *grounds* the whole system.

senses.gloss: To say something in a low, angry voice.
examples: 'Sit down,' he *growled*.
She *growls* at anyone who touches her desk.
He kept *growling* orders from the back of the boat.

senses.gloss: To agree to be responsible for someone else's debt if they fail to pay it.
examples: Her father *guaranteed* the lease.
The government *guarantees* deposits up to a set amount.
The loan is *guaranteed* by the state.

senses.gloss: To speak or write about something with too much enthusiasm.
examples: She *gushed* about the wedding for twenty minutes.
Critics are *gushing* over the new album.
Fans *gush* every time he posts a photo.

senses.gloss: To cut something roughly with heavy blows.
examples: He *hacked* at the frozen ground with a pick.
They had to *hack* a path through the brush.
She was *hacking* branches off the fallen tree.

senses.gloss: To praise someone or something publicly as very good or important.
examples: Critics *hailed* the album as a masterpiece.
He was *hailed* as a hero for weeks.
The papers are *hailing* the deal as a breakthrough.

senses.gloss: To beat an opponent by a very wide margin (informal).
examples: The Lions *hammered* the Bears 41-7.
We got *hammered* in the second half.
They *hammer* every team they play at home.

senses.gloss: To keep a feeling or a thought in your mind for a long time.
examples: She still *harbors* a grudge against her old boss.
He *harbored* doubts about the plan from the start.
They have *harbored* hopes of moving back for years.

senses.gloss: To make someone less kind or less open to feeling, or to become that way.
examples: Two tours overseas *hardened* him.
Opinions have *hardened* on both sides since the strike.
Years of bad news *harden* people.

senses.gloss: To bring a natural force or a resource under control so that it can be used.
examples: The dam *harnesses* the river to make electricity.
Early settlers *harnessed* the wind to pump water.
The company is *harnessing* all that data to price its loans.

senses.gloss: To invent a plan or a plot, usually in secret.
examples: They *hatched* a plan to surprise her at the airport.
The whole scheme was *hatched* over dinner.
He is always *hatching* some new business idea.

senses.gloss: To appear in a place again and again, said of a ghost.
examples: They say a sailor *haunts* the old lighthouse.
The inn is supposed to be *haunted*.
Something *haunted* that house long before we bought it.

senses.gloss: To be the person in charge of a group or an organization.
examples: She *heads* the finance committee.
He *headed* the department for ten years.
The task force is *headed* by a retired judge.
